blocks.x: The numbers

Are Winnipeg rents falling? Through October 2026, month to month, yes, by small amounts. According to [liv.rent's October 2026 Winnipeg rent report](https://liv.rent/blog/?p=69631), published October 6:
The average unfurnished one-bedroom asking rent was **$1,319**, down 0.1% month over month but still up 1.7% from a year earlier.
That was the **third consecutive monthly decline**, and $34 below the July peak of $1,353.

**South Winnipeg** was the most expensive area for one-bedrooms at $1,369 in [liv.rent's August report](https://liv.rent/blog/rent-reports/august-2026-winnipeg-rent-report/), while **St. Boniface** was the lowest at $1,301.

Not everything fell in the October report: East Winnipeg's average two-bedroom asking rent rose about 8% from September to October, to $1,657. That was one month's move, after a dip in September, so treat it as a signal to watch and not as proof of a shortage.

The broader context: [City of Winnipeg data](https://www.winnipeg.ca/news/2026-08-20-winnipeg-leads-major-canadian-cities-housing-growth) shows starts for all housing up 40.4% in the first seven months of 2026 and completions up 52.7%. [CMHC's 2025 rental report](https://eppd1strscr01.blob.core.windows.net/cmhcprdcontainer/sf/project/archive/housing_markets/rentalmarketreportcanadaandselectedmarkets/rental-market-report-2025-fall-en.pdf) says purpose-built rental supply grew 2.6% in the Winnipeg area in 2025.
Our view: "available" is not the same as "chosen"

A flat or falling rent average can hide a split. CMHC's 2025 report says older buildings struggled to compete with newer ones that offer updated features and pricing incentives. Older units with dated finishes can sit longer, and their landlords may end up offering concessions or cutting rent to fill them.
That means the decision facing many Winnipeg landlords is not "should I cut rent?" but "what would it take for this unit to compete with the new building down the street?"
Why new flooring is the first rental upgrade to consider
Heat, drafts and safety items come before any finish. After those, flooring is one of the first things a prospective tenant notices in person and in photos.

Worn carpet, mismatched patches, or scratched laminate make a unit look older than it is. A professional [flooring installation service](/services/flooring) fixes that in a way tenants can see immediately, and modern products hold up for years.

Check what is coming up first. The Province says asbestos was used in buildings built or renovated before 1990, and Health Canada lists floor tiles among the materials, so old tile and adhesive [may need testing](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba) before anyone lifts them.
Pricing smarter
Upgrades and pricing go together. A few principles for a competitive market:
**Know the rule before you price.** In a larger building, a regulated unit's new-tenant rent may be capped, as the note below on the 2027 rules explains.
**Compare with the closest comparable, not the area average.** A renovated unit in South Winnipeg competes with other renovated units, so check what renters are choosing before you set a scope.

**Use upgrades to avoid concessions.** As an illustration only, not a quote: a month of free rent on a $1,319 unit costs roughly $1,300. That money could go toward flooring instead. Get a written quote to compare.
**Time work to vacancies.** Flooring is easiest to install in an empty unit, so plan scopes before a lease ends.
A note on the 2027 rules

Manitoba's 2027 rent guideline is 3%, and from January 1, 2027, the exemption threshold is $2,000, so more units are covered ([Province of Manitoba](https://news.gov.mb.ca/news/?archive=&item=75138)).

When a regulated unit turns over, the rule depends on the building. With four or more units in the complex, a new tenant can't be charged more than the average rent of similar units there. With three units or fewer, the landlord sets the amount.
A landlord-occupied fourplex counts as three. Either way, a Notice to New Tenant is required, with a copy to the Branch within 14 days. Exempt units aren't covered by this rule.

Upgrades won't lift a regulated unit past those limits, but they can still help it lease and keep a tenant. An empty unit is also the easiest time to do the work, which is another reason to complete upgrades before re-leasing, not after.
What the next few months could bring

Winter is often a slower time to lease in Winnipeg, so rents may soften before spring. That can make the next few months a good window to complete upgrades, so renovated units are ready for the spring leasing season.

Watch two numbers. The first is liv.rent's monthly one-bedroom average: if it keeps falling after the three straight declines to October 2026, competition for tenants may grow. The second is your own days-on-market. If dated units are taking noticeably longer to lease than renovated ones, the cost of that vacancy is the clearest argument for upgrading.
The bottom line

Falling average rents do not mean every unit must cut its price. They may mean the market is sorting units by quality. Landlords who upgrade the features tenants notice first, with flooring near the top of the list, are better placed to hold their rents while others discount.
